clarity.justification: The goal and method align: the claim predicts that ablating a small head set will be directionally selective, "degrading false-belief but not true-belief items," while ablating world-tracking heads will produce "the opposite." This is falsifiable because failure to observe that dissociation—or failure of ablation to make the model "default to the true location"—would contradict the stated mechanism, and true-belief stories, move-present/absent stories, and world-tracking-head ablations provide relevant comparisons. However, "rank attention heads by how much they route the pre-move location" does not define the routing metric or candidate-selection rule, and no quantitative effect or decision threshold is supplied, so implementation still requires several analytic choices.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is "Activation patching of the move event to confirm heads carry the belief-world divergence signal" because the source and destination activations, patched components, and divergence measurement are not specified; it is nevertheless custom logic built from standard probing, head ablation, forward-hook, and activation-patching operations rather than an undefined magic step. The required interpretability methods have established tooling, and the proposed Sally-Anne corpus is explicitly constructible from variables including "item, container/location, observer, move event present/absent, order of mention," but the claim names no model, model scale, corpus size, sample count, or other concrete resource figure. The refuting branch is runnable because the design includes "true-belief control stories," varied order and phrasing, zero/mean ablations, and a contrast against "world-tracking heads," although the procedure for identifying those contrast heads also remains underspecified.
